title: Blue-green and rolling deployments
idea: A deployment strategy decides how new code replaces old in production. Blue-green switches all traffic at once; rolling replaces servers a few at a time.

analogy.text: Resurfacing a road. Blue-green: open a second road and redirect everyone. Rolling: close one lane at a time while cars use the others.
analogy.breaks: Software has a hard part roads lack: the data both versions use.

points: Blue-green keeps two full copies: the live one and the new version.
You test the new copy, then switch the load balancer; rollback is switching back.
Rolling replaces instances in small batches, so old and new versions serve together.
Blue-green needs double capacity temporarily; rolling needs little extra but reverts slowly.

steps.caption: The load balancer sends all user traffic to Blue, which runs version 1.
Deploy version 2 to Green. It receives no user traffic yet.
Run checks against Green while users stay on Blue.
Switch: the load balancer now sends all user traffic to Green. Blue keeps running, idle.
Problem found in version 2? Point the balancer back at Blue, which is still running.
Both colours use one database, so each schema change must work for both versions.

code.title: A rolling update
code.caption: Two versions serve together mid-rollout. Return `false` from `healthy` and the rollout stops. Some tools start the new instance first, to keep capacity.

code.title: Kubernetes rolling update
code.caption: Kubernetes, a system that runs containers, rolls out gradually by default. Update the image, watch, undo if needed.

pitfalls: Change schemas in two steps: add first, remove only after the old version is gone.
Add a health check, a request asking if an instance is ready, so rollouts wait.
Let old instances finish in-flight requests before they stop; allow a drain time.

quiz.q: The check fails from the second new instance on. What does this print?
quiz.why: The loop starts a second v2, its check fails, and the loop breaks. The third instance is never touched, so it stays v1.

takeaway: Blue-green switches at once, rolling replaces gradually; plan the rollback either way.
